verdict: OK to lend in Yamunanagar sugar & ethanol — back integrated mills with distillery capacity and digitised cane procurement; avoid pure raw-sugar mills and trader stock finance.
title: Yamunanagar sugar & ethanol: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
The state has raised the cane rate by Rs 15 this season, with the new crop bought at Rs 450 per quintal [1] — that is the single biggest input cost line, so when a proposal lands, check the mill's cane cost against this Rs 450 figure and ask what recovery (quintals of cane per quintal of sugar) it assumes; collect from customer. ## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in the distillery, not the sugar bag.** ICRA notes remunerative ethanol prices and interest subvention on debt-funded distillery capex are what keep cane arrears from piling up, and that ethanol contribution offsets cyclicality for integrated mills [10]. Saraswati Sugar Mills spent about Rs 70 crore in FY2024 on refining capacity, funded from internal accruals, lifting realisations by roughly Rs 0.5-1.0/kg, with no major capex planned after [9]. So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower has ethanol/refining capacity or is a plain raw-sugar mill; if plain, ask what happens to cane payment in a low-sugar-price year. ## What has changed now
**Local news is thin and mostly operational, not financial.** Saraswati Sugar Mills has digitised cane indents for over 20,000 growers ahead of the season [3] — good for procurement discipline, but it tells us nothing about its balance sheet. Separately, the district administration formed eight teams and barred traders from stocking more than 4,000 quintals to curb hoarding [2]. That caps trader inventory, so when a stock-finance proposal from a trader lands, check stock against the 4,000-quintal ceiling; if above, ask for the release order. Peer results are strong but from other companies: Triveni reports improved profitability and reduced debt on sugar and distillery margins [5], and EID Parry's average realisation rose to INR 51.2 per kilogram from INR 43.7 [6]. Rating reports [9][10][11] are undated or old (2024) — treat as background, not current. ## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue integrated mills with distillery capacity and digitised cane procurement; avoid standalone raw-sugar mills and trader stock finance.** Haryana GST collections are running +10.1% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D], a genuine local tailwind. Structure term debt against distillery cash flows with a DSRA, and working capital against sanctioned stock and receivables limits. Take monthly: cane crushed and recovery, sugar stock and realisations, ethanol volumes and prices, cane arrears outstanding, and quarterly debt service cover. Gearing reference from ICRA's FY2024 peer set was 1.4 times, expected to improve to about 1.1-1.2 times [11] — use as a benchmark, not a rule. ## Early-warning signs
**Cane arrears rising month-on-month is the first crack** — it means the mill is funding cane from borrowings. Watch for stock build-up beyond the 4,000-quintal trader cap [2], falling recovery, and any delay in ethanol price notifications. If arrears cross two months of cane value, ask for a fresh cash-flow and consider reducing limits.
